info.description: End-to-end API suite. Select the **VAMS Local** environment, start the backend, then run the whole collection with the Collection Runner (folders run top to bottom). Tokens and ids are captured automatically into collection variables.\n\nAuth: the collection uses `Bearer {{adminToken}}` by default; customer and public requests override it.

item.name: Discounts
item.description: Admin discount/coupon/promotion CRUD, optimistic-lock versioning, and stale-update conflict tests.

exec: const deal = pm.response.json().content.find(d => d.name === 'Buy 4 tyres, save 15%');
pm.test('Discounts expose a version for safe editing', () => pm.expect(deal.version).to.be.a('number'));
// The full PUT body with the version we just read. Extending the end date is a real change (an identical
// save is a no-op and keeps the version) that leaves every price unchanged.
const body = (({name, code, type, value, scope, category, accessoryId, maxDiscountAmount, minQuantity, validFrom, validTo, active, version}) =>
({name, code, type, value, scope, category, accessoryId, maxDiscountAmount, minQuantity, validFrom, validTo, active, version}))(deal);

exec: pm.test('Coupon has an id and code', () => { pm.expect(d.id).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(d.code).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('postmanCouponCode')); });

pm.test('Returns the created coupon', () => { const d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('postmanCouponId'))); pm.expect(d.code).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('postmanCouponCode')); });
